newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish CPN fuel distributor to raise prices Feb 14.
newsitem.headline: Polish CPN fuel distributor to raise prices Feb 14.

text.p: Poland's largest fuel distributor, the state-owned Centrala Produktow Naftowych SA (CPN), will raise fuel prices at filling stations by between five and eight percent on Friday, CPN spokeswoman said.

The move follows a finance ministry decision to free fuel prices and remove all administrative limits on profit margins applied to engine fuel trade in leaded and unleaded petrol and diesel fuel, effective Thursday.
The finance ministry has controlled maximum prices of domestically produced-fuel and distributors' profit margins on imported and domestic fuel.
"Tomorrow we will start to put some order into fuel prices in our filling station network because at the moment, prices differ from station to station," Maria Zawislak-Magrzyk told Reuters.
She said the price of the 95 octane unleaded petrol would rise to 1.55 zlotys (51 cents) per litre from 1.46 zlotys and the price of the 98 octane unleaded petrol to 1.73 zlotys from 1.62 zlotys.
Diesel prices will rise to 1.39 zlotys from 1.29 zlotys, while 94 octane leaded rises to 1.59 zlotys from 1.51 zlotys.
In 1996, CPN had 1,365 filling stations out of Poland's close to 4,800 stations. It sells 50 percent of all petrol sold in Poland and 50 percent of all diesel fuel.
